summary: All seven acceptance criteria are met, but the fix covers one of the three jobs it names, so this fails. Tests I ran: 6 of 6 `check_outcome_state` unit tests pass and 11 of 11 `refusal_corpus` tests pass. Athena's records show fmt, clippy and the full test suite passed. With the fix reverted, the new unit tests do not compile and 7 corpus cases fail. The replay of 50 accepted readings found 0 newly refused. Only the four expected files changed. The problem: the request asked to prevent the whole failure class. The check fires only when a request opens a sentence, line or bullet with publish, deploy, share or release. Of the three jobs the changelog says were 'read that way', only 20261014-082328-g6vy has such a verb. The requests of 20261014-174815-7bf8 (ladder) and 20261017-173508-0wtc (ontology) have none, so the check never fires for them or their retries. The changelog therefore overstates what is fixed, and the reading wrongly said 20261017-173508-0wtc was covered. Smaller problems: the out_of_scope escape matches part of a word, so 'shared helpers' satisfies a share request. Words like 'tag' and 'url' let a criterion pass without naming any delivered state. Requests like 'Build the docs and publish them' are not checked at all. To pass, either correct the changelog and decision text to say the fix covers delivery verbs only (one of the three jobs), or widen the check to cover the other two jobs.
